summary: ITERATION 1 BLOCKER RESOLVED. Real browser owner login through preview ingress now succeeds. Full end-to-end re-test executed: 39 backend pytest tests pass (34 original + 5 new security/lockout, 1 skipped by design), plus complete admin browser flows (create via URL, real multi-chunk upload of 2.4MB PNG, preview, edit, active/deactivate/reactivate, delete cancel+confirm, logout+revocation, forged sessionStorage cannot bypass lock, booking status Pending↔Confirmed persisted across reload with legacy 2 bookings preserved, Call/WhatsApp hrefs use +91 correctly). Visual requirements verified: navbar tagline 'Symbol of Purity' in gold rgb(152,114,36)/#987224 Jost font, footer copyright ends 'All rights reserved.', public hero/footer stays Marathi. Mobile 390px has zero horizontal overflow across public store, admin lock, admin dashboard, admin bookings table. Brute-force lockout (5 wrong attempts → 429 for 15min) verified via loopback in test_security_extra.py (identifier auto-cleaned). Untrusted Origin AND untrusted Referer both server-side rejected via direct 127.0.0.1:8001 tests (bypasses ingress rewrite). Trusted-origin-with-missing-Referer path succeeds (matches real browser). Final DB state clean: 0 products, 0 media, 0 uploads meta, 0 login_attempts, only 2 legacy bookings preserved (NAJ-HIIE9T, NAJ-5PSONR).
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py login() still uses request.client.host as brute-force identifier; behind the preview ingress this collapses to the shared edge IP so a real attacker could lock out the whole edge. Consider deriving from X-Forwarded-For leftmost after trusted-proxy allowlist. Not blocking for QA.
storage.upload_chunk() idempotent replay returns pre-write `received` value — cosmetic, unchanged from iter1.
models.Upload stores full chunk bytes in Mongo — 8MB image inflates docs before delete-on-complete; TTL protects worst case, but GridFS/object storage would be cleaner.

Legacy bookings to preserve: NAJ-HIIE9T, NAJ-5PSONR.
rca of the issue: Iteration1 blocker resolved: backend/.env now sets CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS to a comma-separated list containing both the external preview URL and the internal cluster host to which the Cloudflare worker rewrites Origin. auth.py::csrf_guard checks membership in that set for both Origin and Referer (parsed via urlsplit) while still requiring the X-CSRF-Protection: 1 custom header. Verified end-to-end through the browser (login/refresh/logout all 200) and via direct loopback tests that malicious Origin/Referer are still rejected 403.
